instructions: For the Black Garlic Bearnaise Sauce
Preheat a small pot over medium heat. Add the vinegar, shallot, and about half of the tarragon. - ¼ cup white wine vinegar - 1 shallot peeled + chopped - 1 tbsp tarragon chopped + divided
Bring the mixture to a simmer, the continue to cook until only about 1 tablespoon of liquid remains, about 3-5 minutes. Turn off the heat and set aside to cool to room temperature.
In a medium metal bowl, combine the cooled shallot mixture and the egg yolks. Whisk to combine, then place the bowl over a simmering water bath. - 2 large egg yolks
Whisk constantly while the sauce cooks over the water bath. Continue cooking until the sauce has thickened and turned pale in color, about 5-7 minutes.
Slowly stream in the melted butter while whisking constantly. - 12 tbsp unsalted butter melted
Once all of the butter has been incorporated, turn off the heat and season the sauce to taste with salt and pepper. - To taste kosher salt - To taste freshly ground black pepper
Stir in the remaining tarragon and crushed black garlic clove. - 1 tbsp tarragon chopped + divided - 1 clove black garlic crushed
Serve immediately.
For the Confit Leeks
Prepare a large pot or tub of water with an immersion circulalor. Set the temperature to 185 °F.
Fill 6-8 ice cube tray slots with the olive oil. Freeze for 2-4 hours or until the oil is firm enough to unmold from the tray. - ½ cup extra virgin olive oil
Rinse the leeks in a large bowl of clean water, then pat them dry.
Transfer the leeks, preserved lemon, garlic, and frozen olive oil to a vacuum sealable bag. - 3 leeks trimmed + halved - 3 ½ slices thick preserved lemons - 2 large garlic cloves smashed
Vacuum seal the bag, then transfer to the prepared water bath.
Sous vide the leeks fro 40 minutes.
Remove the leeks from the vacuum sealed bag. Pat try, then preheat a yakitori grill or grill plate over high heat.
Grill the leeks sliced-side down for 3-5 minutes, then flip and cook for an additional 3-5 minutes or until the leeks are well browned on each side.
For the Pistachio-Crusted Lamb Chops
Preheat the oven to 400 °F with convection.
Season the lamb with kosher salt. - ½ rack lamb frenched - As needed kosher salt
Preheat the oil in a large skillet. Add the lamb and sear on all sides. - 2 tbsp cooking olive oil
Allow the lamb to rest while you prefer the crust.

In a medium bowl, combine the breadcrumbs, parmesan cheese, and rosemary. Toss to combine then transfer the mixture to a shallow baking dish or plate. - ½ cup panko breadcrumbs - Parmesan Cheese - Rosemary
Brush the lamb chops with the dijon mustard, then coat them in the breadcrumb mixture. - 1 tbsp dijon mustard
Transfer the rack of lamb to a grill rack placed in a sheet tray. Roast the lamb until the internal temperature reaches 120 °F.

Slice the lamb into individual chops, then serve with Confit Leeks, Black Garlic Bernaise, and garnish with pickled chile peppers and microgreens. - Confit Leeks (see recipe above) - Black Garlic Bernaise (see recipe above) - Pickled chiles chopped - Radish microgreens
